steps.editorState:
• Money is a sensitive subject.
  • All families have different ideas about what they want to talk to children about.
  • These activities are designed to start conversations - but it is up to you to decide what to tell children.
  • Children are curious - and have no idea that some questions might be too personal.
  • There is no need to talk about anything you don't want to.
  • This may be a good opportunity to teach them how to talk about money politely and sensitively.
  • Asking a question back can be a good way to return the conversation back to them.

Deflecting tricky questions

It can sometimes be tricky when children ask question that you don't feel comfortable answering.

Here are some possible responses:

Q: How much money do you have?

How much money people have is usually something they keep private.  

It's also quite complicated for grown ups - it changes all the time so there isn't a simple answer.

Adults bank accounts can also be complicated. You can have different accounts for different things.

We have enough money for what we need.  

Questions to ask back:

  • What do you think adults need to pay for with their money?  
  • Do you know how much money you have in your money box? 
  • Can you think of good ways to keep track of how much money you have?
  • Why do you think adults keep money in bank accounts and not in money boxes?

Q: How much do you earn?

People's salaries are often private. Exact amounts are not something people usually share.  

When you are talking to people, they may think it was rude to ask them about how much they earn.  

There isn't one number to say how much you are paid as money is taken off for Tax and Pensions and National Insurance and Student loan payments before you even get it.

I earn more now than I did when I worked at . . because I have more responsiblity and have to work at the weekends more.

I earn less now that I did when I worked at . . but I have more time at home with you and don't have to travel as far.

Questions to ask back:

  • What kind of job would you like to do? Why?
  • Which do you think will be more important to you - salary, a good work-life balance or doing a job you enjoy?

What to do:

Look at this diagram of an adult bank account.

Now work together to write, draw or talk about where the money goes and how.

No need to talk about amounts

For example:

  • transferring money for rent
  • using a bank card in the supermarket for food.
  • moving money to a saving account
  • getting cash out of an ATM.
  • writing a cheque for swimming lessons.
